question.text: Two resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mi>Ω</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mi>Ω</mi></math> are connected in series with a battery of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and negligible internal resistance. A voltmeter is used to measure voltage across <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mi>Ω</mi></math> resistance, which gives reading as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The resistance of voltmeter must be _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ω</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Voltage across 200 Ω=4-1=3 V.

Therefore, current through the battery, 3200

Now, equivalent resistance of RV & 100 Ω,=Rv100Rv+100

For voltmeter, Rv100Rv+100×3200=1

⇒3Rv=2Rv+200

⇒Rv=200 Ω
